title_en: Commentary on al-Mughnī al-Mufīd — Tape Eleven
body_ar: باب ما جاء في النشرة، عن جابر أن رسول الله (ص) سئل عن النشرة، فقال: هي من عمل الشيطان، رواه أحمد بسند جيد وأبو داود وقال سئل أحمد عنها فقال ابن مسعود يكره هذا كله، النشرة هي حل السحر بما يشبه السحر أو بسحر آخر، وقد اختلف فيها أهل العلم، فذهب جمهورهم إلى تحريمها وأنها من السحر،
body_en:
'Chapter: what has come concerning al-nushrah.' On the authority of Jabir: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about al-nushrah and said, 'It is from the work of Satan.' Narrated by Ahmad with a good chain of transmission (sanad jayyid), and by Abu Dawud, who said: Ahmad was asked about it and said, 'Ibn Masud used to hold all of this disliked (yakrahu).'

Al-nushrah is the undoing of sorcery by something resembling sorcery, or by another act of sorcery. The scholars have differed over it. The majority of them held it to be forbidden (taḥrīm) and held it to be a kind of sorcery,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: وقال سئل أحمد عنها فقال ابن مسعود يكره هذا كله
options: Ibn Masud used to hold all of this disliked (yakrahu)
Ibn Masud used to disapprove of all of this
Ibn Masud used to hold all of this prohibited
flags.note: HIGH RISK. The corpus fixes makrūh as 'disliked', but in the usage of the Companions and the early Hanbalis karāhah very often carries the force of taḥrīm, and Ibn Masud's karāhah in particular is standardly read that way. The Sheikh reports Ahmad's words without resolving which sense is meant. Option 0 keeps the corpus convention but risks understating a reported position; option 2 states a ruling the Arabic does not state. This must be settled by a qualified reviewer, not by the translator.

flags.context: وقد اختلف فيها أهل العلم، فذهب جمهورهم إلى تحريمها وأنها من السحر
options: The majority of them held it to be forbidden (taḥrīm)
Most of the scholars went to the position that it is forbidden
The majority held to its prohibition
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. This is a position attributed to the majority, and the page breaks off immediately afterwards — before the Sheikh states the other position, and before he gives his own. This page therefore contains NO ruling by the Sheikh on al-nushrah. The English must not be presented in a way that lets a reader take 'forbidden' as his fatwa. Recommend the site suppress or prominently caveat this excerpt until the full text is available.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
A ruling text truncated mid-statement. The scholars' disagreement is opened and only the majority position is given; the Sheikh's own position is not in the written source. See the flags.
النشرة has been kept in transliteration because the Sheikh supplies his own definition in the next sentence.
The grading 'with a good chain' is the base text's, reported by the Sheikh, and has been preserved exactly; no grading has been added or dropped.
The site links this tape and tape thirteen (article 510) to the same document, L18.docx; one of the two links is likely wrong on the source site.
